newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary bourse up despite overall E.European trend.
newsitem.headline: Hungary bourse up despite overall E.European trend.

text.p: Hungarian share prices bucked a steady to bearish trend elsewhere on central European bourses and rose mainly on the back of Wall Street's gains.
Polish shares were virtually steady, Czech, Slovenian and Slovak shares closed lower, Romanian stocks were stronger, while Zagreb was mixed.
The Central European Share Index (CESI), which measures price movements in 73 Hungarian, Polish, Czech, Slovak and Slovenian stocks, dipped minimally.
BUDAPEST
The Hungarian share market rose nearly four percent this week bolstered by Wall Street's gains and fresh news about the upcoming global placement in oil company MOL shares.

"We certainly see the impact of the Dow," said Bank Austria Investment Rt's Geza Raner. "MOL attracted attention to the country and first quarter results are coming soon with possible speculation on these."

Hungary's privatisation agency said it would offer 12.5 percent in a global offering in MOL shares, leaving 2.5 percent for over-allotment, to be followed by the domestic offer of a one percent stake to be raised by another one percent in overdemand.
WARSAW
The Warsaw Stock Exchange stayed virtually flat this week and analysts said a lack of strong fundamental signals might keep the market moving sideways next week.
Analysts said that relative equilibrum reached after six weeks of falls would prevent prices from either significant falls or strong gains.

"The prices on the bourse seem adequate to the fundamental value of firms...I believe the market might stay in horizontal trend as so far there are no signals to push it either way," said Roman Sosnowski of Bank Staropolski brokerage.
Some analysts said, however, a strong short-term uptrend might start as early as next week with some prospective low-caps, now trading at 15-20 times historical earnings, leading the rises.
PRAGUE

Czech shares traded on low volumes throughout the week with most dealers focusing on a government announcement on Wednesday aimed at boosting growth, cutting the trade deficit and restoring credibility to the much maligned Czech capital markets.

In the week to Friday the PX50 index was slightly down and dealers said prices would probably continue to stagnate until measures to more firmly regulate the equity market actually come into force. "We have heard this discussion for quite a long time...I think that a market reaction could be seen only after some real results," said Karel Ruzicka of ING Barings.
BRATISLAVA

Small volumes, low foreign interest and expectations of the forthcoming annual meetings this week again plagued the the Bratislava Stock Exchange and kept it in the bearish mood from the previous week.
The 16-share official SAX index fell for the fifth successive session by a total 9.01 points, or 4.42 percent, to close at 194.78 points on Friday.

Brokers said they did not expect the sluggish trade and downward trend to change significantly until the annual meetings of major BSE companies scheduled for the end of this month and the beginning of May.

"But as this is a usual cyclical development before AGM's, traded volumes and prices may rise slightly a few days before meetings of the main companies," said Bohus Betko of ING Barings, adding this may happen within two weeks time.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares fell 1.2 percent this week, as the blue-chip SBI index fell 16.18 points to 1,334.60 on Friday.

Traders said stagnation on the market will continue until foreign capital returns as domestic investors do not have enough money to support constant growth on the market that expects new listings next month.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks closed mixed on Friday with activity picking up and with drugs firm Pliva stealing the spotlight after it announced good 1996 business results.
Market watchers said top shares were likely to forge ahead slightly in lively trade next week.
BUCHAREST
Romanian share prices, which traded mixed early in the week, picked up on Thursday with the start of a bullish mood, sending two independent indices to year highs.
Turnover, high at around 4.0 billion lei on each of the week's first two days of trading, dropped to 3.2 billion on Thursday due to a smaller number of orders accumulated in the market.
Investors focused on the first tier throughout the week, with trading on the second tier remaining subdued.
